column1: # Nevers-Birago Cipher (1572), reconstructed by S. Tomokiyo from the decipherment attached to BnF fr.3251
# no.87 (f.178, Birago to the Duke of Nevers, 8 Sept 1572). Transcribed KEY-IMG-3251, 27 Sept 2026, from the
# hand-drawn table image NeversBirago.png (embedded in nevers.htm, fetched from cryptiana.web.fc2.com/code/,
# see sources/cryptiana/web/manifest_2026-09-27-keyimg.tsv), by two independent blind Sonnet subagent reads
# (each shown only the image, no context), mechanically merged; disagreements settled by this worker's own
# look at the image. Two sub-tables: a letter grid (a-z minus j/k/v/w, plus "et?") and a word-code grid
# (che, per, qual, quello, carmagnola, turino, bugonotti). "sign" describes the hand-drawn mark's shape
# (glyphs cannot be typed). Grade AB = both blind passes agreed on this cell's position and rough shape;
# grade M = this worker settled a disagreement between the two passes.
# One real disagreement settled: the two-circles-joined-by-a-bar ("dumbbell") mark and the three-humped
# cursive 'm' mark -- one blind pass placed the dumbbell under column y (and left z's row1 unmentioned);
# the other placed it under column z (and called y blank). Pixel-cropped the header's own white-text glyph
# x-centers to get exact column-cell boundaries (not just centers) and overlaid them on a 3x zoomed crop of
# the x/y/z/et? region (scratch crop, not committed): both marks sit inside the z column's cell, and y is
# genuinely blank. Recorded here as grade M for the z-column rows and the y blank row.
